title: Astrid and the Witness Again
premise: Marguerite Zhou, archivist of Saint-Aubin's Cathedral, is hired by a nervous stranger to prove that a murder will not happen — a killing the client insists is fated to occur in the cathedral's sealed crypt before the statute of limitations on an old crime expires. Digging through thirty-year-old parish records, Marguerite finds a death certificate for someone still alive: Elias Vann, the man whose 'murder' was staged in 1994 and never reported. As Marguerite maps alibis across three decades, they discover the client is Elias himself, planning to finally die properly so his found family — the people who hid him — can inherit without fear. The climax comes when the real killer from 1994, now the cathedral's beloved dean, corners Marguerite in the crypt; the resolution sees Elias testify at last, the crypt opened, and Marguerite, once determinedly invisible, accepting a place among the witnesses who saved them.
about_author: Odile Ravensworth spent nine years cataloguing municipal archives in a coastal city where half the records were water-damaged and the other half were lies. She writes mysteries about people who mistake paperwork for safety.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid for Nothing
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Marguerite Zhou. A hooded figure leaves an envelope of cash and a single request: prove that no murder has happened yet, and prevent it. Marguerite, who prides themselves on closable cases, almost refuses — then notices the payment includes a key to the cathedral's own locked crypt. Emotional beat: wary curiosity masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Ledgers of the Sealed Door
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. They inventory the crypt's contents against parish ledgers and find a gap: a burial recorded in 1994 with no body ever interred. The name, Elias Vann, appears nowhere else in the archive. Emotional beat: the thrill of an anomaly, quickly shadowed by the sense of being watched in their own stacks.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: Marguerite reconstructs the night of October 12, 1994, cross-referencing choir schedules, visitor logs, and a fire drill that emptied the cathedral at exactly the wrong hour. Everyone's story fits too neatly. Emotional beat: professional satisfaction curdling into suspicion that the record itself was curated.

chapters.title: The Dean's Warm Welcome
chapters.summary: Dean Ambrose Fetter invites Marguerite to tea, charming and generous, asking oddly specific questions about the 1994 files. Marguerite lies smoothly and hates how easily the lie comes. POV alternates briefly to Fetter's assistant, who notices the dean's hands shaking. Emotional beat: dread dressed as civility.

chapters.title: A Woman Called Sister Ilsa
chapters.summary: Marguerite tracks down Ilsa Brandt, retired sacristan, who remembers Elias Vann as a homeless young organist the congregation quietly sheltered. She also remembers the night he 'left' — and the smell of lye soap in the crypt stairwell. Emotional beat: grief surfacing after decades of silence.

chapters.title: The Statute Clock
chapters.summary: Marguerite consults a weary lawyer, learning the manslaughter statute expires in eleven weeks — meaning whoever staged the murder has been safe for thirty years, but whoever might kill Elias now would be too. The client's phrasing suddenly makes terrible sense. Emotional beat: cold clarity, the case reordering itself.

chapters.title: Envelope Number Two
chapters.summary: Second payment arrives with a photograph: Elias Vann alive, older, standing outside a bus depot two towns over. A note reads only 'He wants it done properly this time.' Marguerite realizes the client may be protecting Elias — or hunting him. Emotional beat: vertigo as ally and threat blur.

chapters.title: Bus Depots and Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Marguerite travels to find Elias and instead finds a trail of assumed names, each abandoned like shed skin. A pawnshop owner describes a quiet man who paid to engrave a date on a pocket watch: October 12. Emotional beat: tenderness for a stranger built entirely from other people's memories.

chapters.title: What Ilsa Kept
chapters.summary: Ilsa gives Marguerite a shoebox: Elias's letters, unsent, describing the man who threatened him in 1994 — a description that fits Dean Fetter perfectly. She admits she helped hide Elias and has hated her silence ever since. Emotional beat: confession as relief and burden shared.

chapters.title: The Choir Loft Alibi
chapters.summary: Marguerite tests Fetter's 1994 alibi against acoustics: from the choir loft, he could have seen the crypt door while appearing visible to the whole nave. The perfect alibi was geometry all along. Emotional beat: intellectual triumph undercut by fear of what knowing means.

chapters.title: Invisible No More
chapters.summary: Fetter confronts Marguerite gently, offering a donation to the archive and a warning wrapped in kindness: some doors are locked because what's behind them belongs to everyone's peace. Marguerite declines for the first time in their career. Emotional beat: the cost of visibility, paid willingly.

chapters.title: The Client Revealed
chapters.summary: Marguerite sets a trap using the crypt key as bait; the client takes it. He is Elias Vann himself, gaunt and dying, who hired Marguerite not to prevent his murder but to prove the first one happened — so his testimony could outlive him. Emotional beat: pity and fury braided together.

chapters.title: Elias's Account
chapters.summary: Elias narrates 1994: Fetter caught him stealing candle money for food, beat him, believed him dead, and staged the burial record to bury the sin. Ilsa smuggled him out. He has lived unrecorded since — no name, no grave, no family. Emotional beat: devastating quiet dignity.

chapters.title: Why Not the Police
chapters.summary: Marguerite pushes Elias toward the authorities; he resists, fearing that without corroboration his word dies with him, and that Ilsa and others who sheltered him will be prosecuted. Marguerite promises to build the corroboration instead. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance becoming genuine trust.

chapters.title: Paper Trail, Human Chain
chapters.summary: Marguerite gathers the found family: Ilsa, the pawnshop owner, a former choirboy now a notary, each holding one fragment. Together the fragments form a chain no single witness could. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh — belonging assembled piece by piece.

chapters.title: The Dean Sermonizes
chapters.summary: Fetter delivers a sermon on forgiveness that is unmistakably aimed at Marguerite, quoting the archive's duty to preserve peace over truth. Half the congregation weeps; Marguerite watches Ilsa's face harden into resolve. Emotional beat: public menace, private courage answering it.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: With the statute expiring, Marguerite races to authenticate the 1994 ledger page, discovering Fetter's signature on the burial entry — a document only the killer could have filed. But the original page has been swapped. Emotional beat: desperation, the ground shifting under everything.

chapters.title: The Forger's Hand
chapters.summary: Marguerite identifies the swap: ink, paper stock, and a filing stamp error point to Fetter's own hand, done recently — meaning he knew someone was looking. He is cleaning house. Emotional beat: hunter realizing the quarry has been hunting back.

chapters.title: Into the Crypt
chapters.summary: Lured by a forged message in Marguerite's name, Elias goes to the crypt alone. Marguerite realizes the trap too late and descends after them as Fetter seals the door. POV tightens to breath and dark. Emotional beat: terror stripped of all professionalism.

chapters.title: October Twelfth, Again
chapters.summary: Climax. In the crypt, Fetter confesses freely — the statute protects him — but Marguerite reveals the recording running since the door closed, and that conspiracy to obstruct and evidence tampering carry no such expiry. Ilsa arrives with police she summoned hours ago. Fetter breaks. Emotional beat: justice arriving not as thunder but as arithmetic.

chapters.title: A Name in the Register
chapters.summary: Resolution begins: Elias gives his formal statement, files to restore his identity, and asks Marguerite for one thing — to enter his true name in the cathedral register at last. Ilsa stands witness. Emotional beat: tears earned honestly; a life written back into existence.

chapters.title: The Unlocked Door
chapters.summary: Epilogue. The crypt opens to the public as a memorial; Marguerite, offered the dean's vacant trust seat, accepts instead a modest plaque as 'finder of record.' They keep the archive, but no longer hide inside it. Final line echoes the client's first request: nothing here has happened yet — and now, anything might. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not stumbled into.
